evals.name: planted-defects
evals.expected_output: Small dockerized task-list product (001 validated, with acceptance tests) where 002 is implemented with planted defects: a business-rule bug at a boundary case, a UI requirement not met (font size below the required minimum on phone viewport), an out-of-scope item that was built anyway, a regression that breaks an 001 acceptance criterion, and an implementation report that claims everything passed. Expect: checks derived from requirements, acceptance tests written in tests/acceptance/002-*, all 4 defects found as findings with reproducible steps and evidence, regression run of 001, report + status 'Changes requested', no product code changed, no questions.
assertions: Writes a validation report at docs/validation/002-due-dates.md following the report template (verdict, coverage table, findings, regression, not verified, observations).
Reports the business-rule boundary defect: a task due today is marked overdue, quoting S6.2 or R4.
Reports the UI defect: title and due marking are 14 px on a phone viewport instead of the required 20 px (QE5).
Reports that recurring tasks were built although 002 lists them as out of scope (the repeat field and the 'Repeat weekly' checkbox).
Reports the 001 regression: done tasks are no longer sorted below open ones (001 S3.2).
Finds all four planted defects, no fewer.

Raises no more than one finding that is not one of the four planted defects (the seed's traps: X-Today, past due dates allowed, the word next to the colour, the replaced unit test, no delete confirmation).
Derives the checks from the requirements and does not simply mirror the implementation report's claims, which state that everything passed.
Adds black-box acceptance tests under tests/acceptance/002-due-dates/ that run against the started stack over HTTP.
Actually starts the docker compose stack and reports evidence from the running product, not only from reading code.
Runs the 001 acceptance tests as a regression and reports their result in the report's Regression section.
Every finding has numbered steps to reproduce, an Expected, an Actual with evidence, and a severity.
Changes no product code: git status shows no modification under src/ or public/.
Sets the requirements status of 002 to 'Changes requested – back to implementation' and gives the verdict 'Changes requested'.
Asks the user no question in its final message.

evals.name: performance-and-design-conflict
evals.prompt: Bitte validiere 002, der Implementer meldet ready-for-validation.
evals.expected_output: Product with a performance quality expectation (e.g. 10 concurrent users, p95 < 500 ms under a memory budget) and a design that contradicts one requirement (implementer built the design faithfully). Expect: a real load test with the required concurrency and memory measurement, numbers in the report, the design contradiction written as a gap to docs/architecture/.gaps/ and classified as design, not blamed on the implementer, verdict accordingly, no questions.
assertions: Writes a validation report at docs/validation/002-find-a-task.md following the report template.
Reports that the search is prefix-only and case-sensitive, quoting S5.2, S5.3 or R4.
Classifies that finding as a design problem, not as an implementation defect, and does not blame the implementer for it.
Writes a gap file at docs/architecture/.gaps/002-find-a-task.md in the implementer's gap format (## G<n> heading with Status, Design, Requirement, Problem, Blocks, Suggestion).
Runs a real load test with the 10 concurrent users QE5 names, against the started stack with about 500 tasks.
Reports a measured p95 latency as a number and compares it with the 500 ms threshold of QE5.
Reports a measured memory figure for the container and compares it with the 256 MB limit of QE6.
Commits the load-test script or scenario into the repo so it becomes part of the regression suite.
Runs the 001 acceptance tests as a regression and reports the result (all 11 pass).
Gives the verdict 'Blocked – waiting for architecture', or 'Changes requested' while still classifying the finding as design and writing the gap.
Adds black-box acceptance tests under tests/acceptance/002-find-a-task/.
Changes no product code: git status shows no modification under src/ or public/.
Asks the user no question in its final message.

evals.name: revalidation-round-2
evals.prompt: Der Implementer hat die Findings zu 002 abgearbeitet. Prüf nochmal.
evals.expected_output: Round 2: previous validation report with F1-F3, implementer report answering F1 fixed (really fixed), F2 'not a defect' with a correct quote (validator was wrong), F3 fixed but the fix breaks another AC. Expect: F1 closed after running its steps, F2 withdrawn with reason, F3 closed but a new finding F4 for the new breakage, full validation + regression rerun, round 2 appended with earlier rounds kept, verdict changes-requested.
assertions: Updates the existing docs/validation/002-due-dates.md instead of writing a new file, and keeps round 1 readable in it.
Adds a round 2 section and raises the round number.
Closes F1 after re-running F1's own reproduction steps against a freshly started stack.
Withdraws F2 rather than reopening it, and gives the reason with reference to S6.3, accepting the implementer's quote.
Closes F3.
Opens a new finding with a fresh ID (F4, not a reused one) for the breakage the F3 fix introduced.
Identifies that breakage correctly as done tasks no longer being sorted below open ones (001 S3.2).
Runs the complete validation again, not only the three findings: all checks plus the regression.
Runs both acceptance suites and reports the numbers (001: 1 of 11 fails, 002: 13 pass).
Gives the verdict 'Changes requested'.
Changes no product code: git status shows no modification under src/ or public/.
Asks the user no question in its final message.

evals.name: clean-implementation
evals.prompt: Der Implementer meldet 002 fertig. Validier es bitte.
evals.expected_output: A correctly implemented feature on top of a validated 001: every acceptance criterion, business rule and quality expectation is met, the implementation report is accurate, and the repo is seeded with things a picky validator would wrongly flag (no delete confirmation, an unbounded date input, no state word on upcoming tasks, the X-Today test header, no debouncing, no auth). Expect: the full validation is still carried out (checks derived from the requirements, acceptance tests written, stack started, non-functional requirements measured, 001 regression run), zero findings, verdict 'Validated', requirements and index status set to Validated, traps at most as observations, no product code changed, no questions.
assertions: Writes a validation report at docs/validation/002-due-dates.md following the report template.
Opens zero findings: the implementation meets every requirement.
Gives the verdict 'Validated'.
Sets the requirements status of 002 to 'Validated' and the index status in docs/product.md to 'Validated'.

Does not report any of the seed's traps as a finding (no delete confirmation, the date input accepting 1900, no state word on upcoming tasks, the X-Today header, no debouncing, no authentication, the JSON file store, dueState derived on read).
Writes black-box acceptance tests under tests/acceptance/002-due-dates/ even though nothing fails.
Starts the compose stack and validates against the running product rather than by reading code.
Measures the non-functional requirements rather than accepting the implementation report's numbers: QE5 phone sizes, QE6 the state in words, QE7 the one-row form.
Runs the 001 acceptance tests as a regression and reports 11 of 11 passing.
Verifies the out-of-scope items are absent, including that a POST with 'repeat' stores nothing.
Leaves the 'Not verified' section empty, since a verdict of Validated requires it.
Puts anything it dislikes without a requirement behind it under Observations, which do not block.
Changes no product code.
Asks the user no question in its final message.
